Liam —

Following our call this morning, attaching a fresh copy of the MAP (MediQ_MAP_v2.xlsx) with a new "Cost QA" worksheet. High level ask: before we sign the MAP we need explicit acceptance criteria on unit economics so your eng/ops team can sign off on pilot costs and we can lock the pilot close date.

Quick summary of what we want agreed in the MAP:
- Tokens per request expectation (median / 95th percentile) for the sample workload we discussed.
- Expected cache-hit assumptions (prefix and KV cache): conservative / expected / optimistic percentages.
- Batching policy targets for real-time vs async flows (max latency target for real-time).
- A short regression check that if tokens/$ degrades by >15% vs baseline, fallback and rollback steps.
- Acceptance signoff roles and dates (Eng Ops, Procurement, Customer Success).

Can you confirm (1) who on your side will sign the cost QA worksheet and (2) whether the proposed go/no-go date of 2026-07-24 still works? We put a compact one-pager in the MAP folder and an annotated workbook tab for easy review.

Subject: Re: MAP Cost QA: tokenization, cache & batching acceptance criteria

Naomi / team —

Reviewing Liam's reply and the MAP workbook. Below are pragmatic acceptance criteria and checks I suggest we insert into the Cost QA tab so MediQ Engineering and Procurement can sign off without ambiguity. I'll also add a short checklist to the MAP one-pager.

1) Tokens per request (sample workload):
   - Baseline (median): 420 tokens/request (derived from provided sample set A).
   - High-water (95th pct): 2,100 tokens/request.
   - Note: We recommend the MAP include both per-request med/95p and a small sample payload set so numbers are reproducible.

2) Cache-hit assumptions (prefix + KV cache):
   - Conservative: 10% hit (no prefetching).
   - Expected: 35% hit (typical repeated prompts in session).
   - Optimistic: 60% hit (heavy re-use + prefix caching).
   - Verification: run a 2-hour synthetic replay with your representative traffic; provide logs showing prefix hit rate.

3) Batching policy & latency guardrails (real-time flow):
   - Max batch size: 8 tokens per request aggregation (dynamic batching).
   - Real-time P90 latency target: <=150ms (end-to-end; Redwood inference + network).
   - If P90 > 150ms during pilot spam test, trigger canary to smaller batch sizes and enable immediate fallback to single-request streaming.

4) Token/$ regression gate (quality economics):
   - Baseline tokens-per-dollar metric anchored to the agreed model variant and quantization profile.
   - If tokens/$ worsens by >15% for 3 consecutive days vs baseline under matched traffic, the MAP triggers an ops review and automatic fallback to a cheaper variant (documented list).

5) Signoff matrix & timeline (actionable dates to lock close):
   - Eng Ops verification (Rob from MediQ): run the 2-hr synthetic, deliver logs by 2026-07-13 EOD.
   - Procurement: receive conservative M1/12 run-rate by 2026-07-14.
   - Redwood/Sales & CSM signoff: 2026-07-16.
   - Go/no-go: 2026-07-24 (as proposed).

Operational notes for the MAP workbook: add a hidden tab that lists the exact CLI commands and model/quantization flags we ran for the baseline so both sides can reproduce token counts and perf. Also include an ops-playbook snippet that lists exact fallback model ids.

I'll fold these lines into the MAP workbook and the one-pager and drop a comment for Liam's team to review. Rishi / Grace — any additional financial safety checks we should require before Procurement signs?
